subject.title: feat(gateway): add context engine control API

question: Should OpenClaw core expose a generic context-engine control contract now, and should that contract be HTTP-only or a first-class Gateway RPC surface too?
rationale: This is an additive but public plugin/Gateway control surface with an admin mutation path; code review can identify defects, but maintainers need to own the API shape and security boundary.

options.title: Sponsor after narrowing and fixes
options.body: Keep the PR open, decide the intended API surface, then require handler/advertising, error-handling, docs, and conflict fixes before merge.

options.title: HTTP-only private bridge
options.body: Accept the direct HTTP route idea but remove advertised RPC descriptors until maintainers intentionally add RPC handlers and docs.

options.title: Pause the core API
options.body: Close or defer this PR and keep context-engine maintenance control in owner plugins or a broader control-plane design until the contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after narrowing and fixes
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, decide the intended API surface, then require handler/advertising, error-handling, docs, and conflict fixes before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway method work and current-line ownership make this the best available routing owner for the Gateway API shape decision.
